walkthroughs.h2: The law of demand and supply
walkthroughs.body_html:
Demand slopes downward — buyers buy more as price falls (income & substitution effects).

Supply slopes upward — higher prices reward extra cost of producing more.

Both laws assume ceteris paribus; movements along a curve come from price; shifts come from any other determinant.

Equilibrium is where Qd = Qs.

If P > P*: surplus → suppliers cut prices → P falls.

If P < P*: shortage → buyers bid → P rises.

Shifts: a rise in income shifts demand right for normal goods (left for inferior). New technology shifts supply right.

Consumer surplus = area above price, below demand — what buyers would pay minus what they did.

Producer surplus = area below price, above supply — what sellers received minus minimum acceptable.

Total surplus is maximised at equilibrium — the welfare basis of competitive markets.
